done.why: I had six treasures locked in the trophy case and my score was 120. The maze had worn me out. I had to leave the gold coffin behind because it was too heavy, and I'd never have been comfortable going down past that thief again. Keeping what I had safe felt like the right place to stop.

about: There's a white house above a big underground world. You go down into the dark, take beautiful things out of it, and carry them back up to the trophy case in the living room so they're safe. Getting back up is the hard part: the trap door slams shut behind you, the chimney only lets you carry one thing, and a quiet man with a bag wanders around taking stuff. Lots of passages just end in black water, a closed dam, or rubble that's still falling.

ending.what: No ending. I stopped with 6 treasures in the trophy case (platinum bar, painting, jeweled egg, sceptre, ivory torch, bag of coins) and a score of 120 out of 350.

moments.note: I typed "can I go around the house?" like I'd ask a person. It said "That sentence isn't one I recognize." Then "walk around the house" worked fine.
"open the window wider" got "You can't see any such thing", while I was looking right at the window. Plain "open the window" worked.
The trap door crashed shut behind me and someone barred it. Creepy, and it made me worry about how I'd get out.
I killed the troll in two hits. Then black fog came and his body was gone.
Northeast along the chasm, the path just runs down into cold black water and I came back with wet feet. A lovely way to say no.
"take the platinum bar" came back as "Bar bar ...". The room was echoing my own words back.
I guessed "echo" after saying hello, and the room went quiet. I got the bar. It felt clever.
The chimney said it had room for me, my lamp and one thing more. So I packed everything into the sack and climbed up. A real little puzzle about getting treasure home.
"Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it." I liked that it told me which thing was the problem, but I had to give up the sword, and I never could carry the coffin.
I was stuck below the dome with the rope out of reach, so I tried "pray" at the altar. It sent me up to a sunny forest!
I climbed a tree on the way home and found a jeweled egg. Lucky.
In the maze a man with a large bag wandered through, found nothing worth taking and left disgruntled. I'd left the coins lying there on purpose without realizing it.
The maze was miserable. Every room had the same name, going back the way I came didn't lead back, and I typed directions over and over until "east" dumped me into the Troll Room by accident.
The thief was leaning against the chasm wall with a stiletto, guarding his bag. I didn't dare fight him without my sword.
I closed the trophy case on six treasures. Finally they felt safe.

wished: I wished I could ask normal questions like "which ways are open?" or "why is my sword glowing?" and get an answer, instead of "That sentence isn't one I recognize."
I wished it remembered which maze rooms I'd already been in, or let me mark them somehow. They were all called "Maze".
I wished I could drag or push the gold coffin, or find any way at all to get it home.
I wished I could climb back up the rope in the Torch Room. Dropping down felt like a one-way trap.
I wished I could talk to the man with the bag, or make a deal with him.

lines.line: the path runs down into water, black and still and very cold, and your light finds no other side to it. You go back the way you came, with wet feet.
lines.why: It's a dead end, but it reads like a place. It made the caves feel big and a bit scary.

lines.line: Somebody has sorted the near end of the rubble into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest.
lines.why: Who did that? A small mystery that made me think someone else lives down here.

lines.line: the sound of a great deal of water being held back by something that would rather not be disturbed.
lines.why: It made a locked door feel alive and a little threatening.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: It told me the rule plainly, and that turned getting home into a puzzle I could solve.

lines.line: Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.
lines.why: It told me exactly what to drop. Helpful, though it hurt to leave the sword.

lines.line: A "lean and hungry" gentleman just wandered through, carrying a large bag. Finding nothing of value, he left disgruntled.
lines.why: This was the first sign of the thief, and it made me want to get my treasures home quickly.

fun.why: Getting the bar with "echo", packing everything into the sack for the chimney, and praying my way out of the temple were all real fun. The maze (turns 132-180) dragged it down.

engagement.why: The barred trap door and the thief gave me a real reason to keep my treasures safe, and I cared about getting them back to the case.

difficulty.why: Most puzzles I could work out by trying ordinary things. The fussy wording early on (turns 4, 7) and the maze (turn 176) were the hard parts. The maze was hard in a tedious way more than a clever one.

interestingness.why: The blocked passages each had their own little story: water, a closed dam, rubble someone had sorted into heaps. The rule about what fits up the chimney made carrying things home an interesting problem.

prose.why: The new bits of writing, like the wet feet, the dam that would rather not be disturbed, and the 'not an inch besides', are vivid and a bit funny. Some places only gave the room name when I came back, which felt thin.
